output.brief: The August dip was almost entirely a cooling failure, not a contractor or kiosk problem. The east-side chiller serving floors 6-8 failed on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August. Rooms ran at 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores on those floors recovered to 8.4 once the chiller was repaired. Floors 1-5 stayed flat overall. Of the 74 negative comments, 56 were about heat, and all of those came from floors 6-8. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and kiosk check-in scores did not move, so serving notice on Orrin or pulling the kiosks isn't supported. Dropping the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score would hide a real failure. The 6% rate rise may have cost a little value-for-money score on floors 1-5. That drop is only slightly bigger than the usual August dip, so I can't separate the two, and reversing the rise now is premature. Next steps: restore the deferred maintenance on both chillers, hold critical spare parts on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Affected guests already got an apology and a half-night credit, so any further outreach is optional. Keep Orrin and the kiosks. I'm fairly confident in this, and I collected no further evidence.
